statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns a result r, r equals the maximum, over all integer sequences v of length len(nums) with nums[i] - k <= v[i] <= nums[i] + k for every 0 <= i < len(nums), of the number of distinct integers appearing in v. Here v represents the final array after legally choosing, for each index i, to add some d with -k <= d <= k (possibly d = 0).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: The call max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns a result; it does not fail because of arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, 0) returns r, r equals the number of distinct values in nums, that is, the cardinality of the set { nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums) }.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and k = 0.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, r = min(len(nums), 2*k + 1).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= k <= 1000000000; and there exists an integer a such that nums[i] = a for every 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, r = len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= k <= 1000000000; and len(nums) <= 2*k + 1.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, r >= the cardinality of the set { nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums) }.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, r >= min(len(nums), 2*k + 1).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Let lo = min { nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums) } and hi = max { nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums) }. Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, r <= min(len(nums), hi - lo + 2*k + 1).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k1) returns r1 and max_distinct_elements(nums, k2) returns r2, r1 <= r2.
preconditions: nums is an array with len(nums) between 1 and 100000 and every nums[i] between 1 and 1000000000; k1 and k2 are integers with 0 <= k1 <= k2 <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r and max_distinct_elements(nums2, k) returns r2, r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are arrays of the same length n with 1 <= n <= 100000; every entry of both arrays is between 1 and 1000000000; k is between 0 and 1000000000; and nums2 is a permutation of nums (the two arrays have the same multiset of entries, possibly in different orders).

statement: Whenever max_distinct_elements(nums, k) returns r, there exists an integer sequence v of length len(nums) such that nums[i] - k <= v[i] <= nums[i] + k for every 0 <= i < len(nums), and the number of distinct integers appearing in v is exactly r.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 0 <= k <= 1000000000.
